self-raised-or-from-the-depths: E. D. E. N. Southworth was the bestselling American novelist of her century, and this melodrama shows her powers at full stretch. Her hero climbs from the depths of misfortune through pluck, virtue, and no small number of startling twists. Victorian readers devoured such stories by the million; modern readers will find a lively window into what the 1800s loved to read.
our-friend-john-burroughs: Clara Barrus, Burroughs's friend and biographer, paints an intimate portrait of the great American nature writer at his Catskills home, Slabsides. She recalls his conversations, his walks, his humor, and the stream of famous visitors — from Roosevelt to Edison. A warm, personal memoir of a man who taught America to love its birds and woods.
the-two-paths: John Ruskin's Two Paths contrasts the way of art and the way of industry — lectures on beauty's place in modern life. His eloquent plea for the lovely shaped a generation. Art criticism as moral prophecy. His gospel of beauty challenged the iron age of machinery.
